findings.title: 1 broken link: the site links to an address that answers an error
findings.why: A visitor who follows one of these links reaches an error instead of the page promised.
findings.fix: Point each link at a page that exists, or bring the page back (or redirect its old address to where it went).

findings.title: The site's own scripts throw 1 error on 41 pages

where.says: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'querySelector'), on every page but /, /about/

findings.why: An error nothing catches stops the script that threw it: whatever it was doing (a form's checks, a cart, tracking) is left undone. Visitors never report it; it is seen only in the browser's console.
findings.fix: Open the page with the browser's developer tools, read the console, and fix each error where its stack points.

findings.title: 43 pages have no title
findings.why: Search results, bookmarks and browser tabs show the title: pages that share one can't be told apart, and a page without one shows its address.
findings.fix: Give each page a title of its own that names what it shows (in a single-page app, set it on each route).

findings.title: 21 pages have no description for search results
findings.why: Search results show the description under the title; without one, the search engine picks a line of the page, often the menu or a cookie notice.
findings.fix: Give each page a <meta name="description"> of a sentence or two saying what it offers.

findings.title: 4 of the site's own links redirect before they arrive
findings.why: Every click on one of these links costs an extra round trip before the page starts loading, and search engines see one page at two addresses.
findings.fix: Link to each page's final address (with or without its trailing slash, as the server serves it).

findings.title: 4 security headers no page sends

where.says: no page of the site sends Strict-Transport-Security (without it, browsers are not told to keep to https)
no page of the site sends Content-Security-Policy (without it, nothing limits which scripts a page may run)
no page of the site sends X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors (without it, another site can frame the page to trick a click)
no page of the site sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (without it, a browser may guess a file's type from its content)

findings.why: Each header closes off one way the site could be misused (a downgrade to http, a script slipped in, the site framed in another to trick a click). A missing one is a weaker defence, not a sign the site has been attacked; security reviews ask for them, and each costs a line of server configuration.
findings.fix: Add the missing headers in the web server or the CDN (one setting each), starting with Strict-Transport-Security.

findings.title: 3 pages have no main heading
findings.why: Screen reader users jump to the h1 to learn what a page is, and search engines read it as the page's subject; none, or several competing, says neither.
findings.fix: Give each page one h1 naming what it shows; the site's name in the header is not it.

findings.title: 1 of the site's own links in a closed part of the page redirects before it arrives
findings.why: Each is linked only from a part of the page that is closed when it loads (a menu, a tab, an answer that opens on a click, a link shown on hover): the crawler cannot tell whether a visitor opens it, so these are said apart, and as minor. Every click on one of these links costs an extra round trip before the page starts loading, and search engines see one page at two addresses.
findings.fix: Link to each page's final address (with or without its trailing slash, as the server serves it).

findings.title: Requests to 1 host of other sites failed during the crawl, as seen from the crawler's machine and network

where.says: `vimeo.com`: 4 pages asked it for data and the request failed (404); the name resolves from here, so the request failed for another reason

findings.why: A script on the page asked another site's host for data (a third party's logging, analytics or a widget) and got an error or no answer. This was seen from the crawler's own machine and network only: an ad blocker, the region, DNS filtering or the crawler's own network can cause the same failure, and it may not fail for real visitors. The crawl cannot tell whether a page needs the answer. Where the crawl looked the name up from here, the line says so; "does not resolve" is stronger than "the request failed" (the host is probably gone), but it too is seen from here. It stops no build and no test.
findings.fix: If a name does not resolve, the host is probably gone: remove its snippet or tag from the site. Otherwise open the page from an ordinary browser and network; if the request works there, there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: The site publishes no security.txt, the file that tells security researchers whom to contact
findings.why: Researchers who find a security problem look for /.well-known/security.txt to know whom to tell (RFC 9116); without it they may not report it, or report it publicly.
findings.fix: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with a Contact line (an email address or a form) and an Expires line.

findings.title: 5 errors came from a source the crawl could not tell on 4 pages, as seen by an automated visitor: unconfirmed (no script was named as their source); check in a browser

where.says: 2 errors of no known source: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 11 (line 1 column 12)
1 error of no known source: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 11 (line 1 column 12)
1 error of no known source: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 11 (line 1 column 12)
1 error of no known source: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 11 (line 1 column 12)

findings.why: An error whose stack names no script cannot be traced to the site or to another site: "A network error occurred." is the browser's own word for a request that failed, and the crawler blocks fonts, video and ad hosts, and meets bot challenges, that a person's browser does not, so it is not said as the site's.
findings.fix: Open the page in an ordinary browser with the developer tools' network tab and console. If the request fails there too, check the embed's address and the account with that service, or remove the embed. An error that shows in the console there too names its script there: fix it at that line.
